subject: Michael Jordan

facts.text: Jordan played 1,072 regular-season games and 179 playoff games, scoring 32,292 and 5,987 points.
His first NBA game: 16 points Oct 26, 1984 vs. Washington.
His last NBA game: 15 points Apr 16, 2003 at Philadelphia.
His teams went 706-366 in the regular-season games he played and 119-60 in the playoffs.
He averaged 31.0 points in wins and 28.4 in losses.
Career scoring average: 30.12, the highest in NBA history among 1,382 qualified players (400 games or 10,000 points), ahead of Wilt Chamberlain (30.07).
Career playoff scoring average: 33.4, the highest in NBA history (25+ playoff games); next is Luka Dončić at 30.9.
Most 30-point-average seasons in NBA history: Michael Jordan, 8; next best Wilt Chamberlain, 7.
Only 2 players have scored 3,000 points in a season: Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan (Chamberlain 1960-61: 3,033; Chamberlain 1961-62: 4,029; Chamberlain 1962-63: 3,586; Jordan 1986-87: 3,041).
The only season in NBA history averaging 30 points and 3 steals: Jordan's 1987-88 (35.0 ppg, 3.16 spg).
His longest run of consecutive scoring titles: 7.
His widest scoring-title margin: 8.1 points a game over Dominique Wilkins in 1986-87 (37.1 to 29.0).
He led the league in steals per game 3 times: 1987-88 (3.16), 1989-90 (2.77), 1992-93 (2.83).
He led the league in both scoring and steals in the same season 3 times: 1987-88, 1989-90 and 1992-93.

Seasons with 200 steals and 100 blocks in NBA history: 4 — Michael Jordan 1986-87 (236 stl, 125 blk); Michael Jordan 1987-88 (259 stl, 131 blk); Hakeem Olajuwon 1988-89 (213 stl, 282 blk); Scottie Pippen 1989-90 (211 stl, 101 blk).
Career steals per game: 2.35, No. 3 in NBA history since steals were first recorded (400+ games); Alvin Robertson 2.71, Micheal Ray Richardson 2.63 round out the top three.
Seasons averaging 35 points on 48%+ shooting: 5 — Wilt Chamberlain 1960-61, Wilt Chamberlain 1961-62, Wilt Chamberlain 1962-63, Wilt Chamberlain 1963-64, Michael Jordan 1986-87.

Rookies to average 28 points: 7 — Wilt Chamberlain 37.6 (1959-60), Walt Bellamy 31.6 (1961-62), Oscar Robertson 30.5 (1960-61), Kareem Abdul-Jabbar 28.8 (1969-70), Elvin Hayes 28.4 (1968-69), George Mikan 28.3 (1948-49), Michael Jordan 28.2 (1984-85).
In 2001-02, with Washington, he ranked No. 10 in the league in scoring at 22.9 points a game.
In 2002-03, with Washington, he ranked No. 25 in the league in scoring at 20.0 points a game.
His best scoring season: 37.1 points a game in 1986-87 — 3,041 points in 82 games.
His last 50-point game: 51 points Dec 29, 2001 vs. Charlotte.
As a rookie in 1984-85 he averaged 28.2 points, 6.5 rebounds and 5.9 assists, playing all 82 games.
In his final season, 2002-03, at age 40, he played 82 games and averaged 20.0 points.
At 38 and older he scored 40+ 8 times and 30+ 25 times in 142 games.
In 1994-95 he scored 55 Mar 28, 1995 at New York in just his fifth game of the season.
His most 30-point games in a season: 67, in 1986-87. Most 40-point games: 37, in 1986-87.
His most triple-doubles in a season: 15, in 1988-89.
His best shot-blocking season: 131 blocks in 1987-88, as a guard.
His shortest season: 17 games in 1994-95, averaging 26.9 — his first game that season came Mar 19, 1995 at Indiana.
His best steals season: 259 in 1987-88 (3.2 a game).
His most efficient season from the field: .539 in 1990-91, while averaging 31.5.
His best three-point season: .427 on 260 attempts in 1995-96.
He played all 82 games in 9 seasons.
Jordan scored 50+ points in 31 regular-season games — 3% of all his regular-season games.
His regular-season career high: 69 points, Mar 28, 1990 at Cleveland (23-37 FG, 21-23 FT, W).
Jordan scored 50+ points in 8 playoff games — 4% of all his playoff games.
His playoff career high: 63 points, Apr 20, 1986 at Boston (22-41 FG, 19-21 FT, L).
4 regular-season games of 60+ points: 61 Mar 4, 1987 at Detroit; 61 Apr 16, 1987 vs. Atlanta; 69 Mar 28, 1990 at Cleveland; 64 Jan 16, 1993 vs. Orlando.
One playoff game of 60+ points: 63 Apr 20, 1986 at Boston.
Jordan scored 30+ points in 562 regular-season games — 52% of all his regular-season games.
Jordan scored 40+ points in 173 regular-season games — 16% of all his regular-season games.
Jordan scored 30+ points in 109 playoff games — 61% of all his playoff games.
Jordan scored 40+ points in 38 playoff games — 21% of all his playoff games.
Triple-doubles: 28 in the regular season, 2 in the playoffs.
Games with 40 points and 10 assists: 12 — the biggest was 57 and 10, Dec 23, 1992 vs. Washington.
Best shooting night on 20+ attempts: 24-29 (.828), Nov 16, 1988 at Philadelphia, for 52 points.
Most threes in a game: 7, Jan 18, 1990 vs. Golden State (regular season).
His teams' record in his 40-point regular-season games: 121-52.
His teams' record in his 50-point regular-season games: 23-8.
He scored 50 or more and still lost 10 times — the most in a defeat was 64.
He had 5+ steals in 105 regular-season games and 5+ blocks in 6.
Career-high steals in a game: 10, Jan 29, 1988 vs. New Jersey. Career-high blocks: 6, Dec 2, 1986 at Seattle.
Career-high assists in a game: 17, Mar 24, 1989 at Portland. Career-high rebounds: 19, May 14, 1991 vs. Philadelphia.
Jordan had 8 games with 50 points and 10 rebounds.
Games with at least four steals and four blocks: 13.
Most shots in a game: 49 field-goal attempts, Jan 16, 1993 vs. Orlando (27 made, 64 points).
Most free throws made in a game: 26 of 27, Feb 26, 1987 vs. New Jersey.
Most free throws without a miss: 15-for-15, Jan 10, 1987 vs. New Jersey.
14 of his regular-season 50-point games came without a single made three.
He scored 40+ without a turnover 15 times.
He attempted 20+ free throws in 22 games.
Longest run of consecutive regular-season games with double figures: 866, from Mar 25, 1986 to Dec 26, 2001.
Jordan recorded triple-doubles in 7 straight games, Mar 25, 1989 to Apr 6, 1989.
Longest run of consecutive regular-season games with 20+ points: 72, from Dec 29, 1987 to Dec 6, 1988.
Longest run of consecutive regular-season games with 30+ points: 11, from Feb 13, 1987 to Mar 4, 1987.
Longest run of consecutive regular-season games with 40+ points: 9, from Nov 28, 1986 to Dec 12, 1986.
The 866-game double-figures streak ended Dec 27, 2001 at Indiana, when he scored 6.
Longest run of consecutive playoff games with 30+ points: 8 (Apr 23, 1987 to May 8, 1988).
Jordan scored 20 or more in 60 consecutive playoff games, from Jun 2, 1989 to May 11, 1993.
Jordan reached the Finals 6 times and won all 6: 1990-91 vs. the LA Lakers, 1991-92 vs. Portland, 1992-93 vs. Phoenix, 1995-96 vs. Seattle, 1996-97 vs. Utah, 1997-98 vs. Utah.
In 35 Finals games he averaged 33.6 points; he scored 30+ in 23 of them and 40+ in 6.
He scored 40+ in 4 consecutive Finals games (Jun 11, 1993 to Jun 18, 1993).
His Finals high: 55, Jun 16, 1993 vs. Phoenix.
His best Finals series: 41.0 points a game against Phoenix in 1992-93.
In the 6 title-clinching games he averaged 33.7 points (30, 33, 33, 22, 39, 45).
His teams went 24-11 in his Finals games; none of the 6 series went seven (5, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6 games).
His lowest Finals game: 22 points, Jun 16, 1996 vs. Seattle.
He was held under 20 points in just 6 of his 179 playoff games — the lowest was 15.
Playoff series: 30 won, 7 lost. After losing to Orlando in 1994-95, he won his last 12 series.
His highest-scoring playoff series: 45.2 points a game against Cleveland in 1987-88 (won in 5).
His best scoring postseason of 8+ games: 36.7 over 16 games in 1989-90.

His 8 playoff 50-point games: 63 Apr 20, 1986 vs Boston; 50 Apr 28, 1988 vs Cleveland; 55 May 1, 1988 vs Cleveland; 50 May 5, 1989 vs Cleveland; 56 Apr 29, 1992 vs Miami; 54 May 31, 1993 vs New York; 55 Jun 16, 1993 vs Phoenix; 55 Apr 27, 1997 vs Washington.
In Game 7s he was 2-1, averaging 33.7 points.
His highest playoff scoring average in any postseason: 43.7 over 3 games in 1985-86.
His teams swept 9 playoff series.
In the 7 games in which his team was eliminated he averaged 27.1 points.
His teams were swept 2 times: 1985-86 by Boston and 1986-87 by Boston.
His highest scoring average against any opponent (15+ games): 35.6 against San Antonio over 17 games.
His lowest scoring average against any opponent (15+ games): 20.5 against Toronto — 7 of those 19 games came in his Washington seasons.
He scored 50 against 17 different opponents; the most 50-point games against one team was 3, against Detroit.
His most frequent playoff opponent: New York, 27 games, 19-8, 33.1 points a game.
The team he scored the most regular-season points against: Milwaukee, 2,129 in 66 games.
At New York (Madison Square Garden) he averaged 31.8 points over 31 regular-season games and 30.6 in 12 playoff games there.
Home vs road: 30.4 points a game at home, 29.9 on the road.
On the second night of back-to-backs he averaged 29.7 points over 292 games.
All-Star Games: 13, 262 points (20.2 a game), 37 steals.
His best All-Star Game: 40 points in 1987-88.

method: Every regular-season and playoff game Jordan played, his season, college and All-Star totals, and every NBA player-season ever, all from stats.nba.com. Nothing typed in from memory.
Title seasons and Finals series are derived from the game logs: a playoff run that ends on a win ended with a championship.
Scoring and steals titles use the era's qualification (70 games or 1,400 points; 70 games or 125 steals). Career averages use the league's 400-game / 10,000-point bar; playoff averages 25 games.
